name: bodypart-defer

cpu.note: measured as the cascade bodypart-cascade@r7-fast end to end, which is how this part is served; A5.2.3e, round 1's four blocks pooled (11,081 scored stacks, 32 and 64 workers), cold on the client (the storage server held these blocks): 5.21 h for the 544,972-stack frame. big-1 on the CPU at 32 workers, read third, ran 34.3 a second (4.42 h). Before the overlap A5.3 measured 19.5 a second (ims-a53-bp)
cpu.hardware: 64 cores of an AMD EPYC 9745 host, 256 GB of memory, the archive over NFS 4.2; CPU only; nils-bodypart 0.5.0 (the overlap, its start in the workers), CPU build, torch 2.13.0

limits: Runs on the CPU only (LightGBM); a card changes nothing for it
Fitted on dev A (gold-role subjects in no student's training and never in the screen); its threshold chosen on dev B

params.model: LightGBM 200 rounds, learning rate 0.05, 31 leaves, seed 20261005 (stage 1's booster, LightGBM text)
params.inputs: S1's three seeds (top calibrated probability and log-odds distance to each mode's threshold, seed agreement, the spread of the six probabilities), the 44 registry header features, plane, kind, tilt, the fingerprint's slice count
params.learns: whether stage 1's mean answer equals the stored answer in both modes

tested.note: freeze-d3.json (amendment 5); its read-back changed 0 decisions on 56,878 scorings
tested.claim: the freeze's refit reproduced round 3's decisions exactly: accepted stacks on dev B
stage 1 at 0.99 on dev B: accepted share, with 2 fine and 2 coarse disagreements

intended_use: Stage 1's acceptance rule of bodypart-cascade@r7-fast: a stack is answered by S1 where its score is at least 0.99; never served alone
